catalog_quote: Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Wörter auf der Pänultima des Grundwortes. Einsilbige Suffixe, welcher Art auch, übten auf die Lage des Tones keinen Einfluß aus. (p.174) ... Eine dritte Gruppe von Sprachen hat den Ton auf die nunmehrige Pänultima gerückt. Hierher die Sprachen von Paulohi, Batumerah, Sepa, Wolu und die meisten Wemale-Dialekte (einige der letzteren haben den Ton zuweilen noch auf der nunmehrigen drittletzten behalten), sowie der östliche Sapalewa-Dialekt. (p.175) ... Die meisten übrigen Abkömmlinge des SA., darunter das Amahei, Paulohi, die Wemale-Dialekte, das Batumerah, Sepa und Wolu dagegen haben den Akzent auf die nunmehrige Pänultima verschoben (p.175) ... Dagegen rückt der Akzent bei Hinzutritt dieses Suffixes im Saparua, Nusalaut, Amahei, Paulohi, dem östlichen Sapalewa-Dialekt, den Wemale-Dialekten sowie im Sepa auf die nunmehrige Pänultima. ... wetzen Spl. kasá-e, S. asá-i ... ebenso S. kokú-ro „auf dem Kopf tragen“. Die adjektivischen Suffixe am Verbalstamm verlagern im Asilulu, Nuaulu und Hatue den Ton nicht, im Gegensatz zum Paulohi, Sepa und den Wemale-Dialekten. ... rot Paul. kakaú-ri, S. kaú-o | schwarz Nl. méte-ne, Paul. me-meté-ni, S. meté-o | neu Nl. hónu-e, Paul. herú-i, S. horú-o (p.176)

new_statements.translation: A third group of languages has moved the accent to what is now the penultimate syllable. Here belong the languages of Paulohi, Batumerah, Sepa, Wolu and most Wemale dialects [...] (p.175) | Most of the other descendants of Sub-Ambon, among them Amahei, Paulohi, the Wemale dialects, Batumerah, Sepa and Wolu, have by contrast shifted the accent to what is now the penult [when the enclitic possessive is added] (p.175) | By contrast, when this [verbal] suffix is added the accent moves in Saparua, Nusalaut, Amahei, Paulohi, the eastern Sapalewa dialect, the Wemale dialects and also in Sepa to what is now the penult: [...] Sepa asá-i 'whet' [...] Sepa kokú-ro 'carry on the head' [...] Sepa kaú-o 'red', meté-o 'black', horú-o 'new' (p.176)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the whole word as pronounced: the inherited (Ur-Ambon) penult-of-the-base accent is re-computed over the suffixed word, so that a support vowel, an enclitic possessive, a verbal suffix or an adjectival suffix pulls the accent one syllable rightwards onto the syllable immediately before the suffix (asá-i, kokú-ro, kaú-o, meté-o, horú-o). Unsuffixed bases are penult by the general rule (not separately exemplified for Sepa).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Sepa; the neighbouring Nuaulu, Hatue, Asilulu, Hila, Haruku keep the accent on the base penult (antepenult of the suffixed word), Piru/Kamarian lose the support vowel instead. Some Wemale dialects 'zuweilen' keep the antepenult; nothing of the kind is said for Sepa.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, morphologically complex words (noun + support vowel -o, noun + possessive, verb + person/derivational suffix, adjective + suffix). Historical-comparative presentation (1927) based on a field vocabulary of Sepa village recorded c.1910-12 by K. Deninger; no acoustic or synchronic phonological analysis. Corroborated only weakly by the underlined syllables in the 1920 Holle list 238 (Stokhof 1981:87-99, marked 'stress ?').
new_statements.identity_note: Stresemann's 'Sepa' (abbrev. 'S.', p.13) = the vocabulary recorded in Sepa village on the south coast of Seram by K. Deninger during the II. Freiburger Molukken-Expedition (p.2, item '14. Sepa (DEN.)'), i.e. the Sepa dialect of Sepa-Teluti = Glottolog sepa1242 [spb] (village Sepa, Amahai district; Tamilouw is the other Sepa-dialect village per Collins 1983:110 and Loski & Loski 1989:113). Distinct from Stresemann's 'Wolu' (W.) = the western Teluti / Sou Nama dialect, telu1263 [tlt], which he groups with Sepa in the same accent class, and from 'Nuetetu (bei Sepa)' (Nt.), a Nuaulu-area variety. Not to be confused with Sepa of Papua (a different language).

sources.note: Sepa named explicitly ('S. = Sepa', p.13; Sepa vocabulary recorded by Deninger on the 1910-12 Freiburg Moluccan expedition, p.2): p.175 Sepa is in the group that moved the accent to the 'nunmehrige Pänultima' (penult of the word including the support vowel); p.175 b) possessive enclitics shift the accent to the new penult in Sepa; p.176 d) verbal suffix -ke/-i and adjectival suffixes do the same: S. asá-i 'whet', kokú-ro 'carry on the head', kaú-o 'red', meté-o 'black', horú-o 'new'. Ur-Ambon base rule = penult of the base (p.174).
